questions.text: A COPD patient in moderate hypercapnic respiratory failure is alert and cooperative. Which intervention should be attempted BEFORE intubation?

answers.text: Non-invasive ventilation with BiPAP in S/T mode
Immediate intubation and volume-control A/C ventilation
Nasal cannula at 6 L/min
High-flow oxygen via non-rebreather mask only

questions.text: A patient on BiPAP has an elevated PaCO₂ of 58 mmHg. Which setting adjustment is most appropriate?

answers.text: Increase IPAP to augment ventilation and reduce CO₂
Increase EPAP to improve oxygenation and reduce CO₂
Decrease EPAP to lower baseline pressure and reduce CO₂
Decrease IPAP to reduce the work of breathing

questions.text: A patient's PaO₂ remains low despite adequate IPAP on BiPAP. What adjustment would most directly address the oxygenation deficit?

answers.text: Increase EPAP — it functions like PEEP and directly improves PaO₂
Increase IPAP — higher inspiratory pressure will recruit more alveoli
Switch to S/T mode to guarantee a backup rate
Decrease IPAP to allow more spontaneous effort

questions.text: Which of the following patients has an ABSOLUTE contraindication to NIV?

answers.text: A patient who is apneic
A patient with moderate dyspnea and a PaCO₂ of 55 mmHg
An alert COPD patient who is anxious but cooperative
A post-operative patient with mild hypoxemia

questions.text: How does the design of an NIV device circuit differ from an ICU invasive ventilator circuit?

answers.text: NIV uses a single-limb circuit with no exhalation valve and tolerates continuous air leak
NIV uses a dual-limb circuit with an active exhalation valve
NIV requires compressed gas and electricity; ICU vents are electrically powered only
NIV circuits have larger tubing diameter to reduce resistance

questions.text: A patient on NIV complains of mouth dryness and a dry throat. What is the most appropriate first intervention?

answers.text: Add a heated humidifier to the circuit
Increase the EPAP to improve flow delivery
Switch to a nasal pillow interface
Apply a chin strap to seal the mouth

questions.text: What is AVAPS and how does it differ from standard BiPAP?

answers.text: AVAPS targets a set tidal volume and automatically adjusts IPAP between a min and max range to achieve it
AVAPS sets a fixed IPAP and EPAP that the clinician adjusts manually based on exhaled volume
AVAPS delivers a constant flow rate rather than a constant pressure
AVAPS uses a dual-limb circuit and an active exhalation valve unlike standard BiPAP

questions.text: When initially applying an NIV mask to a patient, which technique minimizes discomfort and improves compliance?

answers.text: Hold the mask to the patient's face before strapping; start at low or zero settings
Apply the mask tightly first, then gradually reduce strap pressure after 30 minutes
Start at full therapeutic settings immediately to quickly assess efficacy
Always begin with a full face mask regardless of patient preference

questions.text: A patient on NIV is a mouth-breather and has an excessive air leak despite correct mask positioning. What is the best corrective action?

answers.text: Apply a chin strap or switch to a full face (oral/nasal) mask
Increase EPAP to 12 cmH₂O to overcome the leak
Switch to a nasal pillow interface
Use the ramp mode to gradually increase pressure

questions.text: In S/T (Spontaneous/Timed) mode on a BiPAP device, what is the primary purpose of the backup respiratory rate setting?

answers.text: To deliver a mandatory breath if the patient fails to breathe within the set interval
To limit the maximum number of breaths per minute the patient can take
To automatically wean the IPAP as the rate increases
To synchronize IPAP delivery with the patient's expiratory effort
